headline: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or after record-breaking 61-goal season, first Englishman in 25 years
summary: Kane's triumph at 33 follows a remarkable career arc, cementing his status as one of football's greatest goalscorers after leading Bayern to a domestic double and England to the World Cup semi-finals.
details: Harry Kane completed his long quest for football's highest individual honour on Monday, winning the Ballon d'Or. The Bayern Munich and England striker achieved this after a record-breaking season, cementing his status as one of the game's greatest goalscorers and becoming the first Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years.

"Wow, wow, wow!" Kane exclaimed after taking the stage, almost speechless. He noted that being in London for the ceremony made the moment extra special, calling it a good omen. He thanked everyone who voted for him, acknowledging the tough competition among world-class players present.

Kane's move to Bayern in 2023 brought him the team trophies that had long eluded him. In the 2025-26 season, he coupled that success with extraordinary goalscoring numbers, making him the leading Ballon d'Or candidate.

The England captain produced the most prolific campaign of his life, scoring an incredible 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern across all competitions. This performance helped the German giants complete a domestic league and cup double. By the end of the season, Kane had established himself as Europe's leading goalscorer.

His influence stretched far beyond club football, as he once again emerged as England's driving force in their World Cup campaign. He scored six goals during the tournament, leading England to the semi-finals with his clinical finishing and defining leadership.

The award represents the culmination of a remarkable journey for Kane. Few players have experienced a career arc quite like his, from struggling to establish himself at Tottenham Hotspur as a youngster to becoming one of the most complete centre-forwards of his generation.

The Ballon d'Or has often rewarded players whose success was built on flair and spectacle. However, Kane's triumph is a tribute to his exceptional consistency, intelligence, and productivity, as he delivered week after week and decided contests match after match.

Kane finished the campaign with an astounding 73 goals for club and country, a total rarely seen in the modern era. More importantly, these goals arrived in moments of genuine significance, helping Bayern collect trophies and driving England deep into the biggest tournament in the sport.

The competition for this year's award was fierce, with Kylian Mbappe breaking World Cup scoring records and Lamine Yamal helping Spain to World Cup glory. Yet, voters ultimately chose Kane, whose excellence lasted the entire season.

At 33, Kane has finally claimed the game's highest individual honour, adding a Ballon d'Or to a legacy that already places him among football's greatest strikers as England's all-time leading marksman and their record World Cup scorer.

Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for the third time, after winning the treble with Barcelona in the 2025-26 campaign, in addition to the Spanish Super Cup. She moved to Women's Super League side London City Lionesses in July after 14 years at Barca.

headline_marked: [[Tarique Rahman to hold summit with Japanese PM Takaichi]] in Tokyo to boost ties
headline: Tarique Rahman to hold summit with Japanese PM Takaichi in Tokyo to boost ties
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is in Tokyo for a four-day visit, aiming to strengthen strategic partnership, trade, and investment with Japan. The high-level talks are set to expand cooperation across key sectors.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is scheduled to hold high-level bilateral talks with his Japanese counterpart, Sanae Takaichi, in Tokyo on Wednesday. The summit aims to strengthen the strategic partnership, boost trade, and investment between the two nations.
The talks are expected to begin at 11:45 AM local time at the Japanese Prime Minister's Office, following a guard of honour for Tarique Rahman. A joint press announcement is scheduled for 12:15 PM.

Discussions will focus on expanding bilateral relations, trade, commerce, and investment, along with Japanese cooperation in various sectors. Both countries' positions on international issues will also be addressed.

Tarique Rahman arrived in Tokyo on Monday morning for his four-day visit at the invitation of his Japanese counterpart. He was received at Narita International Airport by Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Yasutaka Nakasone.

The Bangladesh delegation includes Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Prime Minister's Adviser Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, and State Ministers Humaiun Kobir and Aninda Islam Amit. Prime Minister's Adviser Rehan Asif Asad is also part of the delegation.

Other key members accompanying the PM are Invest Bangladesh Authority Chairman Ashik Chowdhury, Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman, and Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam. Several other secretaries and special assistants are also present.

This marks Tarique Rahman's third overseas state visit since taking office on February 12 last year. Prior to Japan, he made state visits to Malaysia and China, and attended the UN General Assembly in New York.
